events.title: Henry V Triumphs at Agincourt
events.description: Outnumbered English forces under King Henry V defeated a much larger French army in the mud of northern France. Longbowmen played a decisive role in the victory.
events.significance: Agincourt became one of the best-known victories of the Hundred Years' War. It also became a lasting symbol of English martial pride.

events.title: George III Becomes King
events.description: George III took the throne of Great Britain and Ireland after the death of his grandfather, George II. He was 22 years old.
events.significance: His reign lasted nearly 60 years. It covered the American Revolution, the Napoleonic Wars and the union of Great Britain and Ireland.

events.title: The Battle of Balaclava
events.description: British, French and Ottoman forces fought the Russian army during the Crimean War. The battle included the Charge of the Light Brigade, a disastrous cavalry advance.
events.significance: The charge became a famous example of courage mixed with command failure. It was later memorialized in Tennyson's poem.

events.title: Pablo Picasso Is Born
events.description: The Spanish artist was born in Málaga. He grew into one of the most inventive painters and sculptors of his era.
events.significance: Picasso co-founded Cubism and reshaped modern art. His influence is still felt across the art world.

events.title: U.S.-Led Invasion of Grenada
events.description: American forces launched Operation Urgent Fury on the Caribbean island of Grenada. The operation followed a violent coup on the island.
events.significance: It was a prominent Cold War intervention. It ended with the restoration of a civilian government on the island.
